Chapter 7: The Intellectual Love of God—A Higher Form of Understanding.
As your mind grows and you start to really understand the world around you, something remarkable happens. You discover a kind of joy that's deeper than anything driven by wishful thinking or fear. Philosophers have called this the intellectual love of God—or, if you prefer, the intellectual love of Nature.
Now, this isn’t some mystical or supernatural moment. Think of it as a clear, rational appreciation for how everything fits together—the unity and order behind all things. When you realize that everything you see and experience is just a different expression of the same infinite substance, it’s almost impossible not to feel a sense of awe, connection, and genuine love.
But here's what makes this love unique. Unlike ordinary emotions—which often come from desire, fear, or what we hope to get out of a situation—this feeling is grounded in understanding. It arises naturally when you take a step back and notice the sheer necessity and beauty of the world as a whole. Suddenly, you find yourself feeling at home in the universe. The anxiety and sense of not belonging just melt away.
Imagine for a moment that you're standing on top of a mountain at sunrise. The landscape stretches out in every direction, and you’re filled with wonder—not because you own the view, but because you recognize your place within it. That’s what the intellectual love of God feels like: a peaceful, expansive joy that comes from seeing things as they truly are.
So, how do you actually cultivate this kind of love in your own life? There are a few practical steps you can try:
First, spend time contemplating the order of nature. Notice how everything is connected, from the tiniest detail to the widest pattern. The more you reflect on this, the more you’ll see the beauty in the design.
Second, practice gratitude for simply existing. Instead of focusing on what’s missing or what could be better, try to appreciate the miracle of being part of the whole.
And finally, let go of fear and resentment. As your understanding deepens, you’ll notice old anxieties start to lose their grip. They get replaced by a sense of acceptance and sincere appreciation for life’s unfolding.
This kind of love is more than just a fleeting feeling—it’s the highest fulfillment of what it means to be human. It brings a peace and purpose that can’t be shaken by whatever happens outside of you.
When your mind is in sync with the order of reality, you tap into a joy that’s both rational and profoundly moving. And in that space, you’ll find a deep sense of belonging—one that stays with you, no matter what comes your way.
